newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks edge up at open.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks edge up at open.

text.p: Australian shares opened slightly firmer on Friday after metal prices improved and ahead of the full year results of Australia's largest listed company, The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd.
The key All Ordinaries index opened 3.7 points firmer at 2,703.6 but by lunch-time was 4.4 points firmer at 2,704.3.
Market turnover was boosted above the A$1 billion (US$750 million) mark by option expiries with BHP turnover alone topping A$604 million ahead of the Australian end of financial year on June 30.
BHP shares opened slightly weaker but bounced up to be 11 cents up at A$19.17 at lunch after unveiling its profit.
BHP reported a net profit of A$1.39 billion for the year ended May 31, in the middle of the forecast profit range, but before abnormal asset write-downs totalling a massive A$976 million.
"The Dow hasn't offered much in the way of direction so our market could do its own thing today, but so far it has been pretty quiet," a dealer at a Melbourne-based brokerage said.
Resource issues were fairling better than industrials after copper halted its recent slide on the London Metal Exchange and gold improved slightly in New York trading on Thursday.

Leading resource issues was WMC and oil and gas group Woodside Petroleum. WMC shares were 15 cents higher at A$8.53 while Woodside continued its sharp rally since Wednesday to be up 30 cents at A$11.70.
Other blue chip issues were narrowly mixed with banks and transport sectors steady but media, retail and engineering sectors weaker.
